description:
FILED s507b (Opus, 2026-10-04) from member 5's (#2084 (2)) probes; PRE-EXISTING on main 08de9e4f.

REPRODUCER:  $" = "-"; print "[$\"]\n";      perl: [-]      PCL: ["]
perl's toke.c removes the backslash that escapes the string's own DELIMITER before the string body is scanned for
variables (S_tokeq / scan_str), so `"$\""` is the two characters `$"` and interpolates the list separator.  PCL's
interpolation scanner sees `$\` + `"`.  `"[$\,]"` agrees (both print [,]).
Interpolation scanning lives in Pl/InterpScan.pm (standing rule): the fix is where the delimiter-escape is undone,
before InterpScan, for every delimiter (qq{..}, qq(..), "..."): probe `qq{$\}}`? (perl: `$}` is not a variable --
measure), `"$\""`, `"@\""`, and a `\"` NOT after a sigil (unchanged).
Probe file: worktree agent-abf54c6d69793c324 scratch/s507b/m5/i.pl.
subject: SILENT WRONG (PRE-EXISTING): in a double-quoted string, `$\"` (the escaped delimiter after `$`) is perl's `$"` interpolated -- perl strips the backslash before the delimiter first -- PCL prints a literal `"`
